item.title: Paper: PANDA - Prototype-Anchored Alignment for Partially Unpaired Multimodal Learning, with Applications to Alzheimers MRI and TCGA Pathology
item.description: This framework allows models to learn from incomplete multimodal medical data by using auxiliary information to guide training, improving performance without requiring extra inputs during inference.

item.title: Paper: Repair or Resample? Rethinking Failure Debugging in LLM Multi-Agent Systems
item.description: The authors investigate whether debugging multi-agent LLM systems actually fixes underlying issues or just relies on random sampling, providing a framework to test true causal repair.

item.title: Paper: PlanSightRAG: A Visual-First Multimodal RAG for Automating Question Answering and Compliance Checking for Civil Standard Plans
item.description: This visual-first RAG framework automates civil engineering compliance by reasoning directly over 2D plan images rather than relying on error-prone text extraction.

item.title: Paper: Planetary Prediction Engine: Autonomous Geospatial Prediction via Intelligent Data Selection and Foundation Model Embeddings
item.description: This autonomous system streamlines geospatial modeling by using natural language to automatically discover, fuse, and process fragmented environmental data for predictive analytics.

item.title: Paper: BrowserForge: Scaling Web Episode via Parallel Browser Sandboxes
item.description: This framework enables large-scale generation of web interaction data by running parallel browser sandboxes, helping developers train more robust pixel-based web agents.

item.title: Paper: Evidence Blindness in Direct Corpus Interaction: Persistent Navigation with AtlasNav
item.description: The authors identify 'evidence blindness' in LLM agents where critical information is missed during document navigation, providing a framework to quantify and improve retrieval accuracy.

item.title: Paper: CAFE: Self-Improving Search Agents Need Co-Evolving Feedback
item.description: CAFE improves search agents by training them to request and integrate corrective feedback during a task, preventing errors from compounding over long trajectories.

item.title: Paper: StepGuard: Learning Step-Level Guardrails with Scalable Supervision and Safety-Utility Balancing
item.description: StepGuard provides a proactive safety layer for LLM agents by auditing individual tool actions before execution to prevent security risks and unauthorized operations.

item.title: Paper: SRPO: Self-Reflective Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon Reasoning
item.description: This method improves LLM reasoning by teaching models to self-critique their own past errors, providing more effective training signals for complex, long-horizon tasks.

item.title: Paper: RAD: Rule-Augmented Relational Anomaly Detection
item.description: This approach detects anomalies directly within relational databases without flattening tables, helping data scientists identify complex issues that depend on multi-table relationships.

item.title: Paper: MediSkill-Evo: Process-Constrained Self-Evolution for Evidence-Grounded Clinical Interaction
item.description: This framework enables clinical AI agents to follow strict medical protocols and evidence-based reasoning without needing to retrain the underlying model.

item.title: Paper: Cross-Domain, Multi-Task Data-to-Text Generation without In-Domain Training Data
item.description: This research provides a way to generate natural language descriptions from structured data across new domains without requiring any domain-specific training examples.

item.title: Paper: Move by Move: Measuring and Steering How LLMs Conduct Psychotherapy
item.description: Researchers created a framework to evaluate how LLMs perform psychotherapy, helping practitioners understand if AI-driven emotional support aligns with professional clinical standards.

item.title: Paper: Re$^3$Cap: Retrieval-Guided Refinement for Image Captioning Enhancement via Reinforcement Learning
item.description: This method improves image captioning quality by using retrieved multi-modal data as a feedback signal for reinforcement learning, bridging the gap between supervised and RL-based training.

item.title: Paper: AUSO: Action-Level Unified Skill Optimization from Internalization to Utilization
item.description: This framework optimizes how AI agents learn and use skills throughout their lifecycle, ensuring that skill-based guidance is applied only when it actually improves decision-making.

item.title: Paper: The Exceedance Design Effect: Effective Sample Size for Thresholds under Clustering
item.description: This paper introduces a statistical method to adjust threshold calculations for clustered data, preventing common reliability errors when using conformal prediction or safety filters in production.

item.title: Paper: MidTool: Mid-training Data Synthesis for Agentic Tool Use
item.description: The authors created a pipeline to synthesize training data for improving how LLMs interact with external software tools, helping developers build more reliable autonomous agents.

item.title: Paper: Break It Down, Pass It On: Cross-Task Skill Transfer in LLM Agents
item.description: This study analyzes how breaking down skills into subtasks versus whole tasks affects an agent's ability to reuse knowledge, providing a roadmap for more robust skill transfer.

item.title: Paper: Electronic Navigational Chart Change Classification
item.description: Researchers developed an automated classification system to identify high-risk changes in maritime navigational charts, reducing the need for manual review and improving safety consistency.

item.title: Paper: G-CARL: Grounded Checklist-Aligned Reward Learning for Patient-Oriented Medical Report Interpretation
item.description: This paper introduces a framework for generating patient-friendly medical report summaries that remain factually grounded, helping data scientists build more trustworthy healthcare communication tools.
